lesson.title: Reactions to the Industrial Economy from 1750 to 1900
lesson.summary: How workers, socialists, and governments responded to industrial capitalism, and how China and the Ottoman Empire attempted reform.
learningGoals: Explain the causes and effects of calls for changes in industrial societies.
Explain how some states attempted reforms in response to industrial powers.
lesson.bigIdea: Industrial capitalism produced workers' movements, socialist ideas, and government reforms, while states facing industrial powers attempted reforms of their own.
lesson.context: Long hours, low wages, and dangerous conditions led workers to organize. Thinkers debated whether reform or revolution was the answer.

sections.title: Workers and reform

blocks.text: Luddites smashed machines in Britain between 1811 and 1816. Over time, workers formed labor unions to bargain for better wages and hours. Chartists demanded voting rights for all men.
Britain's Factory Act of 1833 limited child labor, and voting rights expanded in 1867 and 1884.

sections.takeaway: Workers organized, and governments gradually responded with reforms.

sections.title: Socialism and Marxism

blocks.text: Socialists argued that workers or society as a whole should own the means of production. Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published the Communist Manifesto in 1848, arguing that history was a struggle between classes and predicting a workers' revolution.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Harsh factory conditions and inequality led critics to argue that capitalism itself must change, which produced socialist and communist movements.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Not all socialists were revolutionaries. Many sought change through elections, unions, and laws.

sections.takeaway: Marxism offered a revolutionary critique of industrial capitalism.

sections.title: Reform in China and the Ottoman Empire
sections.conceptTitle: Reform in China and the Ottoman Empire

blocks.text: China's Self-Strengthening Movement of the 1860s built arsenals and shipyards while keeping Confucian institutions. Defeat by Japan in 1895 exposed its limits.
The Ottoman Tanzimat reforms of 1839 to 1876 reorganized the army, courts, and schools and declared legal equality for all subjects.

sections.takeaway: Reforms in China and the Ottoman Empire borrowed Western methods but faced resistance and limited success.

connections.title: Communism in the 1900s
connections.body: Marx's ideas inspired revolutions in Russia and China in the 1900s, studied in Units 7 and 8.
connections.transferQuestion: Why might Marx's ideas appeal to people in agrarian societies such as Russia or China?
connections.feedback: Connect inequality and revolutionary promises to those societies.
